rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall retention window. This should reveal whether peaks are too early, too late, or compressed, guiding later narrowing of the gradient window and adjustment of slope or temperature.

All compounds eluted well within the gradient, so trim the gradient window to the observed elution window to reduce wasted strong-solvent range and improve time score while keeping similar selectivity. The first peak is not near dead time and the last peak corresponds to only moderate phi_e, so a much lower phi1 should still elute all 10 within 42 min.

The broad window gave perfect resolution but the time term dominates, so now test a steeper gradient to compress the run and see how much the critical mid-eluting pairs depend on slope. This slope probe should show whether CRF can be improved mainly by shortening tG without sacrificing the current resolution margin.

The 10 min gradient is fast but over-compresses the central cluster, while 20 min fully resolves it, so probe an intermediate slope near the apparent optimum. This should improve the critical 5–8 region while likely keeping the run short enough to preserve a strong time score.

The limiting pair improves strongly with shallower slope, and there is still no time penalty at 14 min, so move slightly longer to try to push the 6/7 pair above the apparent scoring threshold. This is the most direct local optimization around the current best method.

Since the critical pair is only weakly resolved near the optimum slope, test temperature to change selectivity rather than slope. A 5 C decrease should modestly increase retention and may reorder or spread the tight 6/7 pair while likely keeping the run in the no-time-penalty region.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity by shifting the overlap to a different central pair, so test the opposite direction to see if modestly higher temperature improves the critical cluster. This isolates temperature effects at the current near-optimal slope without adding a time penalty.

Temperature changes hurt, so stay at 40 C and refine slope on the fast side of the current optimum. Testing 12 min will map the CRF-vs-slope curve around 14–16 min and confirm whether 14 min is truly the best no-penalty operating point.

The central cluster is slope-sensitive and improves monotonically from 10 to 16 min, so test 18 min to see whether the gain in resolution outweighs the added time penalty. This brackets the local optimum between 14 and 20 min more tightly.

At 14 min the last peak still exits around phi_e ~0.55, so the current window is much wider than needed; narrowing the upper end may alter selectivity in the crowded middle without lengthening the run too much. This tests whether keeping all analytes in a more focused composition range can improve the limiting pair beyond the broad 5–95% gradient.

Narrowing the upper end from 0.95 to 0.85 improved CRF and fully resolved the critical pair, so continue trimming phi1 toward the actual elution window. This may preserve full resolution while reducing retention of the last peak and further lowering the time penalty.

The best result came at phi1 0.85, while further lowering to 0.80 hurt the time term despite slightly higher minimum resolution, suggesting the optimum is near 0.85 rather than lower. Test the other side at 0.90 to bracket phi1 and confirm the local optimum.

The 0.90 upper limit improved over 0.85 and 0.95, and the limiting pair remains slightly below full baseline resolution, so combine the best phi1 with the slightly shallower slope that previously resolved that pair. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered without giving up too much of the current no-time-penalty advantage.

At phi1 0.90, 14 min is excellent but the limiting pair is still slightly compressed; testing 12 min will show whether the superior CRF at 0.90 comes mainly from time compression and whether an even shorter run still stays near the top. This cleanly maps the local optimum in tG for the best phi1 found so far.

The best region is clearly around phi1 0.90 and tG 14, so now test whether slightly raising phi0 trims early low-value gradient range without harming the central cluster. This may shorten effective retention and improve the time term while keeping all analytes inside a still-broad window.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 improved CRF further, so combine that with the previously strong phi1 0.85 setting to see if a slightly narrower window gives the last bit of improvement. This is a focused local search around the current best region in phi-space at the proven optimal slope and temperature.

We have already achieved the maximum CRF, so this injection is only to confirm whether the optimum is broad or sharply peaked around phi1 = 0.85. Stepping phi1 one notch lower maps robustness while staying in the same high-performing region.

With the maximum already reached, the remaining useful question is robustness in phi0 around the optimum; raising phi0 one step further will show whether 0.10 is uniquely best or whether the optimum plateau extends upward. This stays close to the best method while probing whether the early low-organic segment is still longer than needed.

Both phi0 = 0.10 and 0.15 at phi1 = 0.85 give the maximum score, so push phi0 one more step to define the upper edge of the optimal plateau. This tests how far the initial composition can be raised before the first peak approaches the unretained region or central selectivity begins to degrade.

The optimum plateau appears to include phi0 0.15 and phi1 0.85, so test the neighboring upper-end composition to see whether 0.15/0.90 is equally optimal or slightly inferior. This helps map the high-CRF plateau boundaries in both phi0 and phi1 around the maximum.

Since 0.15/0.85 is optimal and both higher phi1 and higher phi0 start to erode the margin on the critical pair, test the lower-phi1 side at the same phi0 to complete the local plateau map. This will confirm whether the optimum is centered at phi1 = 0.85 for phi0 = 0.15 as well.

With the maximum already reached, use a remaining run to probe robustness in tG around one optimal composition. Testing 12 min at phi0 0.10, phi1 0.85 checks whether the optimum plateau extends to a faster method or whether 14 min is still the necessary slope for full score.

Since both 0.10/0.85/14 and 0.15/0.85/14 achieve CRF 1.000, test the faster 12 min slope at the other optimal composition corner. This checks whether the slightly higher phi0 tolerates a steeper gradient better while staying near the maximum.

The score maximum is already achieved, so use the last two runs to test robustness of the winning composition to temperature. A +5 C shift at the best composition will confirm whether the optimum is narrowly tied to 40 C or stable enough for routine use.

Complete the temperature robustness check at the winning composition with the opposite 5 C shift. This will confirm that 40 C is the clear optimum and bracket how sharply the critical 6/7 pair deteriorates with temperature.
